newsitem.title: USA: S&P UPS SECURITY-CONNECTICUT CORP RATINGS.
newsitem.headline: S&P UPS SECURITY-CONNECTICUT CORP RATINGS.

text.p: NEW YORK, July 2 - Standard & Poor's today has raised its claims-paying ability and issuer credit ratings of Security-Connecticut Life Insurance Co. and Lincoln Security Life Insurance Co. to double-A'-minus from single-A'-plus, and has raised its issuer credit and senior debt ratings of parent Security-Connecticut Corp. to single-A'-minus from triple-B'-plus.
All ratings are removed from CreditWatch, where they were placed Feb. 24, 1997 upon the announced acquisition of Security-Connecticut by ReliaStar Financial Corp.

These rating actions reflect the successful completion of the $508 million acquisition, which was done as a stock-for-stock transaction and includes ReliaStar's assuming $75 million of Security-Connecticut debt.
These actions place the ratings of Security-Connecticut Corp. and its insurance operations on par with those of ReliaStar and its insurance operations.

With the acquisition of Security-Connecticut, ReliaStar's intent is to broaden its product offerings and better utilize its distribution channels through the cross-selling of products, while simultaneously bolstering its profitability through expense savings.
Security-Connecticut's primary product offerings of single and joint life, fixed universal life, and term life insurance should nicely complement ReliaStar's variable life and annuity products.

Annualized expense savings of approximately $9 million are expected, the equivalent of 17% of Security-Connecticut's 1996 noncommission expense base, through the consolidation of operations. ReliaStar gained experience in integrating company operations with its 1995 acquisition of USLICO Corp..

Including the assumption of Security-Connecticut's debt, ReliaStar's leverage and coverage ratios are supportive of its ratings. After the acquisition, ReliaStar's debt to capitalization is approximately 13%, combined debt plus preferred securities to capitalization is around 24%, double leverage is 116%, and fixed charge coverage during 1997 is expected to exceed 7 times.
The company remains committed to maintaining debt to capitalization below 25%, and preferred securities to capital below 15%.

Standard & Poor's expects capitalization of the combined entity will remain excellent, a strong level of earnings will be generated, and asset quality will remain good. Wednesday, 2 July 1997 16:26:52 ENDS nN02256446
